'''Mark Valentino Ingram Sr.''' (born August 23, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[New York Giants]] ([[1987 NFL season|1987]]–[[1992 NFL season|1992]]), the [[Miami Dolphins]] ([[1993 NFL season|1993]] to [[1994 NFL season|1994]]), the [[Green Bay Packers]] ([[1995 NFL season|1995]]), and the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] ([[1996 NFL season|1996]]). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]]. He is the father of [[Mark Ingram II]], who won the [[Heisman Trophy]] in 2009 and is the [[New Orleans Saints]]' second all-time leader in rushing yards.

'''Mark George Miller''' (born August 13, 1956) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played with the [[Cleveland Browns]] (1978–1979) before being traded in August 1980 to the [[Green Bay Packers]], where he saw no action. He was released by the Packers before the [[1981 NFL season|1981 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1981/08/04/The-Green-Bay-Packers-released-veteran-quarterback-Mark-Miller/6327365745600/|title=The Green Bay Packers released veteran quarterback Mark Miller Tuesday|date=August 4, 1981|access-date=September 11, 2021}}</ref> Miller then briefly resurfaced with the [[Michigan Panthers]] of the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) in 1983.

Miller had put together a solid [[college football|college]] career with the [[Bowling Green Falcons football|Bowling Green Falcons]] (1974–1977), resulting in the Browns making him a third round selection in the [[1978 NFL draft]]. During his brief career his role was that of a [[National Football League depth chart|backup]] quarterback, consequently making his playing time limited. He attempted 47 passes, completed 15 for only 243 yards, seeing the most action in the 1978 regular season finale against the Cincinnati Bengals after replacing an injured [[Brian Sipe]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/markmiller/2521232/profile|title = Mark Miller Stats, News and Video - QB|website = [[NFL.com]]}}</ref>

'''Mark Eric May''' (born November 2, 1959) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for 13 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the 1980s and 1990s. May played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]] and earned [[unanimous All-American]] honors. He was selected in the first round of the [[1981 NFL draft]], and played professionally for the [[Washington Redskins]], [[San Diego Chargers]], and [[Arizona Cardinals]].

May became involved in broadcasting following his retirement from the NFL in 1993. Most notably, he was employed by ESPN between 2001 and 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/college-football/2017/04/81933/espn-lays-off-mark-may-per-report|title=ESPN Lays Off Mark May, Per Report|date=2017-04-27|work=Eleven Warriors|access-date=2017-04-28|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://247sports.com/article/report-mark-may-among-those-laid-off-by-espn-52518190/|title=Report: Mark May among those laid off by ESPN|work=247Sports|access-date=2017-04-28}}</ref>

'''Mark W. Messner''' (born December 29, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the 1989 season. He sustained a serious knee injury in the [[1989–90 NFL playoffs#NFC Championship: San Francisco 49ers 30, Los Angeles Rams 3|1989-90 NFC Championship Game]] against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and never played in another game.

Messner played [[college football]] at the [[University of Michigan]]. He started every game, 49 in all, at [[defensive tackle]] for Michigan from 1985 to 1988.  He was the first position player ever to be selected as a first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] player all four years.

Messner was also a four-time [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]], earning third-team selections in 1985<ref name="AP 1985">{{cite news |title=All-America |newspaper=Akron Beacon Journal |date=December 10, 1985 |page=D2 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5310293/1985_associated_press_allamerica/}}</ref> and 1986,<ref name="FN 1986">{{cite news |title=All-America News: Football News |newspaper=St. Louis Post-Dispatch |date=November 23, 1986 |page=14D|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5716828/allamerica_team_football_news/}}</ref> first-team in 1987,<ref name="TSN 1987">{{cite news |title=Brown TSN top player of '87 |newspaper=Daily Chronicle (DeKalb, IL) |date=December 9, 1987 |page=11 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5713765/brown_tsn_top_player_of_87/}}</ref> and unanimous honors in 1987.<ref name="AFCA 1988">{{cite news |title=1988 Kodak All-America Team |newspaper=Asbury Park Press |date=November 22, 1988 |page=D2   |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5718585/1988_kodak_allamerica_team/}}</ref><ref name="AP 1988">{{cite news |title=AP All-America |newspaper=The Cincinnati Enquirer |date=December 9, 1988 |page=F2 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5718250/ap_allamerica/}}</ref><ref name="FWAA 1988">{{cite news |title=Football Writers Association All-America Team |newspaper=The Indianapolis Star |date=December 2, 1988 |page=C6 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5719267/football_writers_association/}}</ref><ref name="UPI 1988">{{cite news |title=UPI All-America Team |newspaper=The Indianapolis Star |date=December 15, 1988 |page=C10 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5718485/upi_allamerica_team/}}</ref><ref name="WC 1988">{{cite news |title=Walter Camp All-America Team |newspaper=Southern Illinoisan |date=November 24, 1988 |page=18 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/5718700/1988_walter_camp_allamerica_team/}}</ref>

He set still holds Michigan records for [[quarterback sack]]s in a game (5), career [[tackle for loss|tackles for loss]] (70), and career sacks (36). He was inducted into the [[University of Michigan Athletic Hall of Honor]] in 2014.
